title: Ordinary-limit and Roos models for resolved global Hom towers
statement: Use the module-valued representative and resolved-tower functors of [def-sfb-global-rhom-resolved-model]. For every complex L and every K-injective complex I of strict towers whose terms are injective towers, the actual map limit.post:representative(L,lim I)→lim representative(L,I_n) is an isomorphism. Both Q(lim I) and Q(lim representative(L,I_n)) carry derived-limit triangles whose first arrows have exactly the localized ordinary limit projections. The assertion does not include existence of resolutions, K-injectivity, a comparison with global RHom, naturality of such a comparison, or any cohomology equivalence.

proof.text: For an injective tower each transition splits degreewise. The injective-tower Roos theorem gives its distinguished triangle with actual projections, and makes the localized termwise product a categorical product. Transport the triangle along the unique product isomorphism to the selected product in D(R). The first arrow then has precisely the localized limit projections.

Degree q of the global Hom complex is the product over p of Hom(L^p,I^(p+q)). Maps into an inverse limit are compatible families, and products over p and n interchange. Thus representative(L,lim I) is canonically isomorphic to lim representative(L,I_n), with the same differentials and A-action. The isomorphism is exactly limit.post, characterized by its projections.

Split transitions of the original tower induce split surjections on the Hom product terms. To solve x_n-t_n x_(n+1)=b_n, start with x_0=0 and use the chosen transition sections recursively. Hence 1-shift on the product is surjective in each degree, with kernel the ordinary limit. The kernel-to-shifted-cone lemma gives the ordinary-limit Roos triangle. Products of A-modules are exact, so their degreewise product localizes to the derived product. The kernel inclusion has coordinates (0,z); transport to the selected product gives the stated projection equations.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0941, original proof steps 3–4 and the source triangle part of step 2. The statement only asks for the triangles and their projections, so no descent to a separate total-derived-limit functor is needed.

theorem resolved_tower_models
    (L : CochainComplex (Modules.{c, v, max c v r} R) ℤ) :
    (∀ I : (resolvedProperty.{c, v, r} R).FullSubcategory,
      IsIso (limit.post I.obj.asFunctor (representative.{c, v, r, a} R A φ L))) ∧
      (∀ I : (resolvedProperty.{c, v, r} R).FullSubcategory,
        ∃ hp : HasProduct (fun n : ℕ ↦
            DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.obj (I.obj.asFunctor.obj (op n))),
        ∃ (p : DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.obj (limit I.obj.asFunctor) ⟶
            ∏ᶜ (fun n : ℕ ↦ DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.obj (I.obj.asFunctor.obj (op n))))
          (δ : (∏ᶜ (fun n : ℕ ↦ DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.obj
              (I.obj.asFunctor.obj (op n)))) ⟶
            (DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.obj (limit I.obj.asFunctor))⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
          IsDerivedLimitTriangle
            (fun n : ℕ ↦ DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.map
              (I.obj.asFunctor.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op))
            (DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.obj (limit I.obj.asFunctor)) p δ ∧
          ∀ n : ℕ, p ≫ Pi.π _ n = DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.map
            (limit.π I.obj.asFunctor (op n))) ∧
      (∀ I : (resolvedProperty.{c, v, r} R).FullSubcategory,
        ∃ hp : HasProduct (fun n : ℕ ↦ DerivedCategory.Q.obj
            (((representativeTowers.{c, v, r, a} R A φ L).obj I).obj (op n))),
        ∃ (p : (globalHomLimit.{c, v, r, a} R A φ L).obj I ⟶
            ∏ᶜ (fun n : ℕ ↦ DerivedCategory.Q.obj
              (((representativeTowers.{c, v, r, a} R A φ L).obj I).obj (op n))))
          (δ : (∏ᶜ (fun n : ℕ ↦ DerivedCategory.Q.obj
              (((representativeTowers.{c, v, r, a} R A φ L).obj I).obj (op n)))) ⟶
            ((globalHomLimit.{c, v, r, a} R A φ L).obj I)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
          IsDerivedLimitTriangle
            (fun n : ℕ ↦ DerivedCategory.Q.map
              (((representativeTowers.{c, v, r, a} R A φ L).obj I).map
                (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op))
            ((globalHomLimit.{c, v, r, a} R A φ L).obj I) p δ ∧
          ∀ n : ℕ, p ≫ Pi.π _ n = DerivedCategory.Q.map
            (limit.π ((representativeTowers.{c, v, r, a} R A φ L).obj I) (op n)))
